summary: Integration part 1 for brief 5. I ran the app end to end on real data (real API, live loop off, port 8759; Vite 5219). (1) The live flood list was checked one by one against the NWS flood products in effect (37 events: every one is in a listed flood) and the river gauges at minor or worse (every lower-48 one is in a flood; Puerto Rico's tide gauge is out by rule 1). The table, with a check note per flood, is live_list_table below. Two real bundles were built and checked (Rio Grande at Alamosa, CO: river gauge ALAC2 with a West Gulf RFC forecast; Ducktown flash flood: NWS Morristown and Peachtree City Flash Flood Warnings), and the Public overview (Fires and Floods, same camera), the Public flood view, the Command flood view and Forensic were shown on real floods, at 1440x1000, 1024x768 and on a phone. (2) Real data found real problems, fixed with tests: the gauge-only flood at Copperhill, TN (Ocoee River gauge at major) said 'No NWS flood product here right now' while NWS Morristown's Flash Flood Emergency for Copperhill covered the gauge (now a gauge-only flood lists the products over its gauge, attached like a watch); two 'San Juan River flood (UT)' entries 3 km apart (areal warnings now join by the river they name); a flood's id changed with each NWS update after a split, and a live id could be aliased to another (fixed in assign_ids); a gauge in flood under only a watch would be hidden as watch-only; waterbody state and position notes in names; a forecast crest whose time had passed was shown as 'FORECAST CREST' (now 'Highest NWS forecast' in Public, Command, Official now and the chart); the gauge-only circle meaning ignored the backend's outage and tide-gauge caveats; 'No fire open' in Floods; the dock chart cut 'MODERATE 11.0'; a past flood's Forensic card offered a build that answers 409. (3) CONTRACT section 16 now carries every as-built note (16.16 per role, including backend-flood-live, which was fixed during this step) and the resolved deviations (GET /api/floods answers 200 with both lists down; 16.7 route limits; 16.8 rules; 16.10-16.12 signatures; 16.14 all new backend and web strings, now tested against the code; 16.15 OPERA credit). SPEC 8.8 follows the catalog changes; the contract triple's parity test is green. (4) README has a Floods section, the optional EARTHDATA_TOKEN set-up, flood CLI and routes, and a Flood data credits table with terms. Incident: a throw-away debug test of mine ran without the isolation fixture and removed the real data/floods at 09:53 UTC; I moved the remains aside, regenerated fixture-flood and rebuilt the 8 real bundles (all check_bundle 0 problems); the registry history is lost, so some flood ids differ from earlier reports.

live_list_table.note: Checked one by one on the real API (FIRE3D_LIVE=0, port 8759) against the raw NWS flood products in effect (nws.flood_active, the same cached answer the list was built from) and the riv_gauges gauges at minor or worse; first at 09:38 UTC (58 floods with carry-overs, before the fixes) and again at 10:03 UTC after the fixes (39 floods: the registry and last-known summaries were lost in the incident, so no carry-overs). Every NWS product event is in a flood; every lower-48 gauge at minor or worse is in a flood.
changes_made: Toccoa River / Ocoee River flood (CPHT1, Copperhill TN): lists the NWS Morristown Flash Flood Emergency and warnings over its gauge (was: 'No NWS flood product here right now').
Joshua Creek flood (NOCF1): lists the Peace River Flood Warning that covers its gauge (recorded day and live).
San Juan River flood (UT) + (UT, 2) -> one 'San Juan River flood' (areal warnings naming the same river, 3 km apart).
Salt River flood (AZ) + Rio Verde flood (AZ) -> one 'Salt River flood' (adjacent areal warnings, one naming the Salt River).
Toccoa River (GA) / Ocoee River (TN) flood -> Toccoa River / Ocoee River flood (state notes dropped).
Loxahatchee River 500 ft downstream of US 1 flood + Loxahatchee River flood -> one Loxahatchee River flood (position note dropped).
Ducktown flash flood: its id no longer changes with each NWS update (split ids reassigned; a live id is never aliased).

known_issues: Copperhill, TN: the Ocoee River gauge flood ('Toccoa River / Ocoee River flood') and the 'Ducktown flash flood' are one event listed twice (river and flash products never join by distance). Both show the Flash Flood Emergency. Linking a gauge to a Flash Flood Warning whose text names its river would make one river flood, but its Public facts would then show river rows instead of detection and damage threat: a decision for the user.

Gauge-only floods inside another flood's NWS product now take that product's level and circle (e.g. Joshua Creek under the Peace River Flood Warning); the product is the other river's, named verbatim in the product row.

Four gauges forecast to reach minor flood stage with no NWS product (BFFU1 UT, BOWD1 DE, DESI4 IA, PLMF1 FL) are not floods: D2 starts floods from observed readings only. They show as diamonds on the map.
The 'Ducktown flash flood' is named after NWS Morristown's first listed place (TN) while its point and county come from the largest polygon (Fannin County, GA).

Floods that left the lists are not carried over in this container until seen again (last-known summaries were lost in the incident); older flood ids that only the lost registry knew answer 404 here (data/ is local and gitignored).

Command, past floods (from backend-flood-live's note): the model chip says 'could not be loaded' for a not_available_for_past_dates answer; the slim chart labels a past reading with today's category and its age against now.
The fixture server answers every demo flood's evacuations with the New Mexico fixture (older test-tooling issue).
Phones, Command flood view: the map controls take two rows under the title bar (the same layout as Command fire).
The national flood list can name two tide-gauge floods by one place ('Key Largo flood (FL)' and '(FL, 2)').
EARTHDATA_TOKEN path still tested only with a fake token and a mock transport (no real token here).
cut_line_left: Analysis-tab small multiples in Forensic (each gauge has a 'Chart' button that shows it in the dock).
Data-status block in Command's Official now (there is no flood updates feed).
Flood layers' credit lines stay as the key's last line / the foot portal; not folded into lib/dataCredits.ts (they already reach the foot bar).
NASA GIBS picture stays undrawn (web-flood-public's reason: its colours read like a hazard map); the key says 'no usable image' with the backend's reason.
Part 2: live loop and past floods end to end, the Command past-flood seams above, final SPEC check.
